title: Grammatical Endings (-o, -a, -e, -i)
subtitle: Determine part of speech instantly using invariant vowel endings
keyPoint: Every Esperanto root changes its part of speech predictably by changing its final vowel: -o for nouns, -a for adjectives, -e for adverbs, and -i for infinitive verbs.

useCases.label: Naming things (Nouns)
useCases.example: La amiko estas feliĉa.

useCases.label: Describing things (Adjectives)
useCases.example: La rapida hundo kuras.

useCases.label: Describing actions (Adverbs)
useCases.example: Ŝi kantas bele.

examples.en: La patro legas libron.
Tio estas bona ideo.
Li parolas rapide.
Mi volas lerni Esperanton.
La suno brilas varme.

mistakes.note: An adjective ending in -a cannot function alone as the subject noun without an appropriate noun ending or suffix.
Use the adverb ending -e to modify a verb, not the adjective ending -a.
Infinitive verb forms must always retain the -i ending; roots cannot stand alone.

quiz.question: Choose the noun form: 'The ___ is on the table.'
quiz.explanation: Nouns in Esperanto always end with the vowel -o.

quiz.question: Choose the adverb form: 'She sings ___.'
quiz.explanation: Adverbs modify verbs and always end with -e.

quiz.question: Choose the infinitive verb form: 'I want ___.'
quiz.explanation: Infinitives (to do something) always end with -i.

quiz.question: Choose the adjective form: 'A ___ dog runs.'
quiz.explanation: Adjectives describing nouns always end with -a.

tip: Whenever you encounter an unfamiliar Esperanto word, glance at its final vowel to instantly recognize whether it is a noun (-o), adjective (-a), adverb (-e), or verb (-i).

title: Plurality and Noun-Adjective Agreement (-j)
subtitle: Match nouns and their modifying adjectives with the plural ending -j
keyPoint: In Esperanto, both nouns and their modifying adjectives must agree in number by adding -j whenever they refer to more than one person or thing.

useCases.label: Attributive plural
useCases.example: Grandaj domoj staras tie.

useCases.label: Predicative plural
useCases.example: La infanoj estas feliĉaj.

useCases.label: Plural demonstrative
useCases.example: Tiuj libroj estas novaj.

examples.en: La bonaj amikoj venas hodiaŭ.
Ruĝaj pomoj estas sur la tablo.
Tiuj novaj aŭtoj estas rapidaj.
Ni havas multajn pensojn.
La birdoj kantas dolĉe.

mistakes.note: Adjectives must agree with plural nouns by adding -j as well.
Predicate adjectives linked by 'estas' must also take the plural marker -j.
Verbs in Esperanto never take plural endings; only nouns, adjectives, and correlatives do.

quiz.question: Select the correct plural phrase: 'Green trees'
quiz.explanation: Both the adjective (verda) and the noun (arbo) require -j in the plural: verdaj arboj.

quiz.question: Complete the sentence: 'La floroj estas ___.'
quiz.explanation: Predicate adjectives agreeing with plural subjects take -aj.

quiz.question: Choose the properly matched singular phrase:
quiz.explanation: Singular forms do not take -j: 'bela floro'.

quiz.question: Complete the sentence: 'Tiuj knaboj estas tre ___.'
quiz.explanation: The adjective modifying plural boys (knaboj) must end in -aj: 'lertaj'.

tip: The letter 'j' sounds like the English 'y' in 'boy' (-oj) and 'eye' (-aj); pronounce both words with a smooth diphthong.

title: The Direct Object Accusative (-n)
subtitle: Clarify direct objects and unlock free word order with -n
keyPoint: Attach the accusative ending -n to any noun or adjective serving as the direct object of an action, allowing flexible word order without changing the meaning.

useCases.label: Direct object
useCases.example: Mi trinkas varman teon.

useCases.label: Inverted word order
useCases.example: La leteron skribas ŝi.

useCases.label: Agreement in accusative
useCases.example: Ni aĉetis novajn librojn.

examples.en: La knabo legas bonan libron.
Mi amas vin.
Feliĉajn tagojn ni spertis.
La kato kaptis malgrandan muson.
Ŝi trinkas freŝan akvon.

mistakes.note: Both the noun and modifying adjective must receive the -n accusative marker.
Never use the accusative after linking verbs like 'esti' (to be); predicate complements stay nominative.
Adjectives must match both the plural (-j) and accusative (-n) endings in order: -ajn.

quiz.question: Identify the direct object: 'The dog chases the cat.' -> 'La hundo ĉasas la ___.'
quiz.explanation: The direct object receiving the action must take -n: 'katon'.

quiz.question: Choose the correct phrase: 'I see green apples.' -> 'Mi vidas ___.'
quiz.explanation: Both plural and accusative endings combine as -ajn and -ojn: 'verdajn pomojn'.

quiz.question: Choose the correct form: 'Li estas bona ___.'
quiz.explanation: The verb 'esti' takes a nominative complement without -n: 'instruisto'.

quiz.question: Complete the inverted sentence: '___ amas la patrino.' (The mother loves the children)
quiz.explanation: Since 'la infanoj' is the object being loved, it takes both plural -j and accusative -n: 'La infanojn'.

tip: Remember the fixed suffix order: root + noun/adjective vowel (-o/-a) + plural (-j) + accusative (-n). It is always -ojn and -ajn, never *-onj.

title: Simple Verb Tenses (-as, -is, -os)
subtitle: Conjugate every verb seamlessly with three invariant tense endings
keyPoint: Esperanto verbs do not change for person or number; simply attach -as for present, -is for past, or -os for future to the root.

useCases.label: Current action or state
useCases.example: Mi loĝas en granda urbo.

useCases.label: Completed past event
useCases.example: Hieraŭ ni vizitis muzeon.

useCases.label: Upcoming future plan
useCases.example: Morgaŭ ili alvenos frue.

examples.en: Mi nun laboras en oficejo.
Ili promenis en la parko hieraŭ.
Ni renkontiĝos morgaŭ vespere.
Ĉu vi komprenas la demandon?
Ŝi legis interesan libron.

mistakes.note: Do not translate English continuous 'am reading' with 'estas + -as'; simple '-as' already covers ongoing actions.
Verbs never take plural suffixes; they remain invariant regardless of the subject.
Tense changes do not affect case marking; the direct object still requires -n.

quiz.question: Complete with past tense: 'Hieraŭ ni ___ amikojn.' (visited)
quiz.explanation: The past tense suffix for all verbs is -is: 'vizitis'.

quiz.question: Complete with present tense: 'Ŝi nun ___ Esperanton.' (learns)
quiz.explanation: The present tense ending is -as: 'lernas'.

quiz.question: Complete with future tense: 'Morgaŭ la vetero ___ varma.' (will be)
quiz.explanation: The future tense ending is -os: 'estos'.

quiz.question: Which verb correctly fills the blank: 'Ili kune ___ bieron hodiaŭ.' (drink)
quiz.explanation: Current actions occurring 'today' use present -as: 'trinkas'.

tip: Think of the vowel progression chronologically: 'i' (past, behind you), 'a' (present, right now), 'o' (future, round ahead).

title: The System of Correlatives (Tabelvortoj)
subtitle: Form 45 essential pro-words by combining 5 initial letters with 9 endings
keyPoint: Esperanto correlatives are formed systematically by joining an initial element indicating type (ki-, ti-, i-, ĉi-, neni-) to a final root indicating category (-o, -a, -e, -u, etc.).

useCases.label: Asking questions
useCases.example: Kiu estas tiu persono?

useCases.label: Specifying locations
useCases.example: Tie mi trovis mian horloĝon.

useCases.label: Expressing totals and negatives
useCases.example: Neniu scias ĉion pri la mondo.

examples.en: Kio estas sur la tablo?
Mi neniam vidis tian grandan urbon.
Ĉiu homo volas esti feliĉa.
Kie vi loĝas nun?
Tiu libro estas tre interesa.

mistakes.note: Use 'kiu' (individual/which person), not 'kio' (abstract object/thing), when referring to individuals or specific items.

mistakes.wrong: Mi vidas neniun personon tie ĉi.
mistakes.note: 'Neniu' already means 'no one / nobody'; pairing it redundantly with 'persono' is usually unnecessary.
To indicate motion towards a place, add the accusative -n to the location correlative: 'kien' (whither / where to).

quiz.question: Choose the correlative for 'where': '___ estas la stacidomo?'
quiz.explanation: The prefix ki- (question) combined with place suffix -e yields 'kie' (where).

quiz.question: Choose the correlative for 'everyone': '___ volas lerni.'
quiz.explanation: 'Ĉi-' (all/every) + '-u' (individual) gives 'ĉiu' (everyone / each).

quiz.question: Choose the correlative for 'never': 'Mi ___ manĝas viandon.'
quiz.explanation: 'Neni-' (none) + '-am' (time) gives 'neniam' (never).

quiz.question: Choose the correlative for 'what': '___ okazis hieraŭ?'
quiz.explanation: 'Ki-' (question) + '-o' (thing/matter) gives 'kio' (what).

tip: Group correlatives by endings to memorize them quickly: -u (individuals), -o (things), -a (quality), -e (place), and -am (time).

title: Questions with 'Ĉu' and Negation with 'Ne'
subtitle: Form polar questions and negative sentences effortlessly
keyPoint: Place 'ĉu' at the start of a statement to turn it into a yes/no question, and place 'ne' directly before the word you want to negate.

useCases.label: Yes/No Question
useCases.example: Ĉu vi estas preta?

useCases.label: Verbal Negation
useCases.example: Li ne ŝatas kafon.

useCases.label: Selective Negation
useCases.example: Mi trinkas ne teon, sed akvon.

examples.en: Ĉu vi loĝas en Berlino?
Mi ne konas tiun viron.
Ĉu la vetero hodiaŭ estas bona?
Ŝi ne volas dormi nun.
Ĉu vi ne havas tempon?

mistakes.note: To negate the action, place 'ne' directly before the finite verb, not after it.
Esperanto never uses auxiliary 'do/does' to ask questions; simply prefix the sentence with 'ĉu'.
Esperanto avoids double negatives; pairing 'ne' with a negative correlative like 'nenion' is incorrect.

quiz.question: '___ you speak English?'
quiz.explanation: 'Ĉu' is the particle used to form standard yes/no questions in Esperanto.

quiz.question: 'I ___ like cold weather.'
quiz.explanation: 'Ne' precedes the verb 'ŝatas' to express negation without needing auxiliary verbs like 'do'.

quiz.question: 'Is she a teacher?' -> '___ ŝi estas instruisto?'
quiz.explanation: Starting the clause with 'ĉu' turns the declaration into a polar question.

quiz.question: 'We do not work on Sundays.' -> 'Dimanĉe ni ___ laboras.'
quiz.explanation: 'Ne' directly negates the verb 'laboras'.

tip: Think of 'ĉu' as the English 'whether'—it simply marks the whole sentence as a question without altering word order.

title: Accusative of Motion and Direction (-n)
subtitle: Show movement into or toward a place using the -n ending
keyPoint: Add the accusative ending '-n' to a noun or adverb to indicate movement toward a target, distinguishing destination from static location.

cells: La kato saltas sur la tablo.
The cat jumps around on top of the table.
La kato saltas sur la tablon.
The cat jumps onto the table.
We take a walk at home.

useCases.label: Entering a Space
useCases.example: La birdo flugis en la ĉambron.

useCases.label: Onto a Surface
useCases.example: Li metis la libron sur la liton.

useCases.label: Directional Adverbs
useCases.example: Kien vi vojaĝos somere?

examples.en: La muso kuris sub la liton.
Li iris en la ĝardenon por legi.
Mi revenos hejmen vespere.
Ŝi falis en la akvon.
Kien vi kuras tiel rapide?

mistakes.note: The preposition 'al' inherently indicates direction, so do not add '-n' after it.

mistakes.wrong: La hundo kuŝas sur la liton.
mistakes.right: La hundo kuŝas sur la lito.
mistakes.note: Lying on a bed is a static location, not motion toward it; therefore, no '-n' is used.
'Kie' means 'where (at)'; when asking about destination, you must use 'kien' (whither).

quiz.question: 'The boy ran into the house.' -> 'La knabo kuris en la ___.'
quiz.explanation: The movement enters into the house, requiring the singular accusative of direction '-n'.

quiz.question: 'Where are you driving to?' -> '___ vi veturas?'
quiz.explanation: 'Kien' is used for asking toward which destination someone is traveling.

quiz.question: 'The cup fell onto the floor.' -> 'La taso falis sur la ___.'
quiz.explanation: The falling motion terminates onto the surface, which requires the accusative '-n'.

quiz.question: 'We walk in the park (inside it, not into it).' -> 'Ni promenas en la ___.'
quiz.explanation: Because the activity is static within the park and not moving into it, no '-n' is added.

tip: Prepositions like 'al' (to) and 'ĝis' (until/up to) already express direction, so adding '-n' after them is redundant and forbidden.

title: The Volitive Mood (-u)
subtitle: Commands, requests, wishes, and purpose clauses with the -u ending
keyPoint: The verb ending '-u' expresses will, intention, direct commands, polite wishes, and clauses following verbs of desiring or ordering.

useCases.label: Direct Command
useCases.example: Fermu la pordon, mi petas.

useCases.label: Let's (Suggestion)
useCases.example: Ni komencu la lecionon.

useCases.label: Subordinate Clause of Will
useCases.example: Li petis, ke mi telefonu.

examples.en: Legu la libron atente!
Mi petas, ke vi helpu min.
Vivu la paco en la mondo!
Li diris al mi, ke mi silentu.
Ni iru al la kinejo hodiaŭ vespere.

mistakes.note: Esperanto does not use infinitive accusative structures like English 'want you to come'; use 'ke' + '-u'.
After the command 'bonvolu' (be pleased to), the main action must be an infinitive (-i).
Subordinate clauses expressing desire, requests, or commands take '-u', not future '-os'.

quiz.question: 'Open the window!' -> '___ la fenestron!'
quiz.explanation: The '-u' ending forms the imperative mood for direct orders.

quiz.question: 'Let's drink some water!' -> 'Ni ___ akvon!'
quiz.explanation: When used with 'ni', the '-u' verb creates a cohortative suggestion ('Let us...').

quiz.question: 'She ordered that he leave.' -> 'Ŝi ordonis, ke li ___.'
quiz.explanation: Verbs of command require the volitive '-u' in the subsequent 'ke' clause.

quiz.question: 'Please speak slowly.' -> 'Bonvolu ___ malrapide.'
quiz.explanation: 'Bonvolu' itself already carries the '-u' ending; the accompanying verb must be in the infinitive (-i).

tip: Unlike English imperatives which lack subjects, Esperanto often includes pronouns: 'Vi legu!' (You read!), 'Ni manĝu!' (Let's eat!).

title: The Conditional Mood (-us)
subtitle: Hypothetical situations and polite statements with -us
keyPoint: Replace the verb ending with '-us' in both the condition and the result to describe unreal, hypothetical, or polite scenarios.

cells: If you had come, we would have rejoiced.

useCases.label: Hypothetical Scenario
useCases.example: Se mi estus riĉa, mi aĉetus domon.

useCases.label: Polite Inquiry
useCases.example: Mi ŝatus trinki tason da teo.

useCases.label: Wish / Preference
useCases.example: Estus bone renkontiĝi morgaŭ.

examples.en: Se mi scius la respondon, mi dirus ĝin.
Ĉu vi volus promeni kun mi?
Sen via helpo ni ne sukcesus.
Mi preferus resti hejme hodiaŭ.
Se li havus monon, li aĉetus aŭton.

mistakes.wrong: Se mi havos monon, mi aĉetus aŭton.
mistakes.right: Se mi havus monon, mi aĉetus aŭton.
mistakes.note: Hypothetical condition and result must match moods; use '-us' in both parts.
Attach '-us' directly to the modal verb ('volus'), followed by an infinitive (-i).

mistakes.wrong: Se mi estus vi, mi faros tion.
mistakes.right: Se mi estus vi, mi farus tion.
mistakes.note: Do not mix the real future '-os' with an unreal conditional condition '-us'.

quiz.question: 'If I were a bird, I would fly.' -> 'Se mi ___ birdo, mi flugus.'
quiz.explanation: Hypothetical 'if' clauses require the conditional ending '-us'.

quiz.question: 'I would like to order.' -> 'Mi ___ mendi.'
quiz.explanation: 'Ŝatus' softens the desire politely, meaning 'would like'.

quiz.question: 'If you practiced more, you ___ speak better.' -> 'Se vi ekzercus pli, vi ___ pli bone.'
quiz.explanation: The apodosis (result clause) of an unreal conditional statement takes '-us'.

quiz.question: 'Could you close the window?' -> 'Ĉu vi ___ fermi la fenestron?'
quiz.explanation: 'Povus' expresses a courteous and polite request ('could you').

tip: In Esperanto, 'se' (if) takes '-us' directly when the condition is unreal; there is no rule forbidding conditional endings inside the if-clause.

title: The Reflexive Pronoun 'Si' and Possessive 'Sia'
subtitle: Clear 3rd-person reference without ambiguity
keyPoint: 'Si' and its possessive 'sia' refer back exclusively to the subject of the clause and are only used for third-person subjects.

useCases.label: Self as Direct Object
useCases.example: Li vidas sin en la spegulo.

useCases.label: Subject's Own Possession
useCases.example: Petro amas sian edzinon.

useCases.label: After Prepositions
useCases.example: Ili kunportis manĝaĵon por si.

examples.en: Ŝi kombas siajn harojn matene.
Li parolis al si mem.
Johano renkontis Petron en lia domo.
Ili defendis sin kontraŭ la danĝero.
Maria prenis sian sakon kaj foriris.

mistakes.note: 'Si' is only for third persons; first and second persons use 'min', 'nin', 'vin'.
'Sia' can never be part of the subject itself because it must refer to an already stated subject.
'Lian' means someone else's wife; to refer to Petro's own wife, you must use 'sian'.

quiz.question: 'Anna loves her (own) dog.' -> 'Anna amas ___ hundon.'
quiz.explanation: 'Sian' refers back to the subject 'Anna', signifying her own dog.

quiz.question: 'He sees himself in the mirror.' -> 'Li vidas ___ en la spegulo.'
quiz.explanation: 'Sin' is the 3rd person reflexive pronoun in the accusative case.

quiz.question: 'I prepare myself for the exam.' -> 'Mi preparas ___ por la ekzameno.'
quiz.explanation: 'Si' cannot be used with first person 'mi'; use 'min' instead.

quiz.question: 'They took their (someone else's) bags.' -> 'Ili prenis ___ sakojn.'
quiz.explanation: 'Iliajn' means another group's bags; 'siajn' would mean their own bags.

tip: Golden rule: 'Si' or 'sia' can never be the subject of a clause or part of the subject phrase.

title: Core Productive Affixes (mal-, in-, -il-, -ej-, -ar-)
subtitle: Build hundreds of precise words using five essential building blocks
keyPoint: Esperanto derives opposites, female forms, tools, places, and collections by attaching predictable, unvarying affixes directly to root words.

useCases.label: Opposites with mal-
useCases.example: Tiu ĉambro estas tre malgranda kaj malvarma.

useCases.label: Instruments & Places
useCases.example: En la kuirejo mi prenis grandan tranĉilon.

useCases.label: Collectives & Gender
useCases.example: La instruistino montris novan vortaron al la klaso.

examples.en: Li malfermis la pordon per speciala ŝlosilo.
Ni renkontiĝos antaŭ la lernejo posttagmeze.
Granda arbaro ĉirkaŭas la malnovan urbeton.
Mia fratino legas libron en sia ĉambro.
La vetero hodiaŭ estas tre malvarma.

mistakes.wrong: Mi uzas tranĉejon por tranĉi la panon.
mistakes.right: Mi uzas tranĉilon por tranĉi la panon.
mistakes.note: Use -il- for tools and instruments; -ej- denotes a location, so 'tranĉejo' would mean a cutting room.
Use the prefix mal- to express an antonym (small/short), rather than negating with 'ne'.
Use the suffix -ar- to express a collection or set of things (a library of books / set of books).

quiz.question: A place where people work (labori) is called a ___.
quiz.explanation: The suffix -ej- signifies a place dedicated to an action or thing: laborejo = workshop / workplace.

quiz.question: The tool used to write (skribi) is a ___.
quiz.explanation: The suffix -il- denotes a tool or instrument: skribilo = writing utensil / pen.

quiz.question: The opposite of 'helpi' (to help) is ___.
quiz.explanation: The prefix mal- produces the exact semantic opposite: malhelpi = to hinder / obstruct.

quiz.question: A collection of trees (arboj) is an ___.
quiz.explanation: The suffix -ar- forms collective nouns representing an entire group or cluster: arbaro = forest / woods.

tip: Affixes in Esperanto can be stacked freely: 'mal-varm-ig-il-o' means an instrument that makes things un-warm, i.e., a refrigerator!

title: The Accusative of Measure, Duration, and Date
subtitle: Using the -n ending without a preposition for time, distance, and cost
keyPoint: The accusative ending -n replaces missing prepositions to indicate duration of time, points in time, distance, and monetary measure.

cells: en la lundo / je la lundo

useCases.label: Duration of Action
useCases.example: Ŝi atendis la buson tutan horon en la pluvo.

useCases.label: Point in Time
useCases.example: La dek-kvinan de marto ni komencos la kurson.

useCases.label: Distance and Price
useCases.example: Ni kuris du kilometrojn matene.

examples.en: Mi studis Esperanton du jarojn.
Li alvenos la sekvan tagon.
Ili promenis kvin mejlojn tra la arbaro.
Tiu ĉemizo kostas dudek dolarojn.
Ni restis tie tri semajnojn.

mistakes.right: Mi laboris dum tri tagoj. / Mi laboris tri tagojn.
mistakes.note: Do not combine a preposition with the accusative of time; use either the preposition 'dum' or the '-n' ending, not both.
Without a preposition such as 'je', a phrase expressing measure or distance requires the accusative ending -n.
Expressing a specific temporal point without a preposition requires -n on the noun.

quiz.question: Choose the correct phrase: 'We stayed there for one whole week.'
options: Ni restis tie dum tutan semajnon.
Ni restis tie je tutan semajnon.
quiz.explanation: Without a preposition, 'tutan semajnon' takes the accusative ending -n on both the adjective and the noun to show duration.

quiz.question: Complete the date: 'He was born on the fifth of May.' -> 'Li naskiĝis ___ de majo.'
quiz.explanation: Dates indicating 'when' without a preposition take -n: 'la kvinan de majo'.

quiz.question: How do you say 'The ticket costs ten euros' without a preposition?
options: La bileto kostas por dek eŭrojn.
La bileto kostas je dek eŭrojn.
quiz.explanation: 'Kosti' takes an accusative of measure when no preposition is used: 'dek eŭrojn'.

quiz.question: Why is 'Mi dormis dum tri horojn' incorrect?
options: Prepositions like 'dum' should not be followed by -n here.
The plural -j- must be dropped before -n.
quiz.explanation: The accusative replaces a preposition. When 'dum' is already present, the noun stays in the nominative: 'dum tri horoj'.

tip: Think of -n as an invisible preposition; if you already have a clear preposition like 'dum' or 'en', you usually drop the -n.

title: Transitivity and Voice with Suffixes -ig- and -iĝ-
subtitle: Mastering causative '-ig-' (make/cause) and inchoative '-iĝ-' (become)
keyPoint: The suffix -ig- makes any root transitive (causing an action/state), while -iĝ- makes verbs intransitive (becoming or happening on its own).

useCases.label: Causing a State (-ig-)
useCases.example: La varma teo varmigis miajn manojn.

useCases.label: Spontaneous Change (-iĝ-)
useCases.example: La vetero rapide varmiĝis posttagmeze.

useCases.label: Changing Transitivity
useCases.example: Ŝi naskiĝis en Parizo kaj tie kreskiĝis.

examples.en: La forta vento faligis la malnovan arbon.
La folioj fariĝis flavaj en aŭtuno.
Bonvolu fermi la pordon, ĝi ne fermiĝas mem.
Li sidigis la infanon sur la seĝon.
La glacio fandiĝis sub la hela suno.

mistakes.wrong: Mi varmiĝis la supon en la forno.
mistakes.right: Mi varmigis la supon en la forno.
mistakes.note: Use -ig- because you are actively warming the soup (transitive action with direct object).
'Fermi' is inherently transitive (to close something); if the door closes on its own, use -iĝ-.
'Naski' means to give birth; to be born is 'naskiĝi'.

quiz.question: How do you say 'The sun melted (made melt) the snow'?
quiz.explanation: 'Fandigi' is causative (to melt something). 'La neĝo fandiĝis' would mean the snow melted by itself.

quiz.question: Choose the correct verb: 'Post longa tago, mi finfine ___ laca.' (I became tired)
quiz.explanation: To become tired is 'laciĝi' (-iĝ- indicates entering a state). 'Lacigi' means to tire someone else out.

quiz.question: Verbs with the suffix '-iĝ-' are always ___.
options: transitive and require an accusative object
intransitive and never take a direct object
quiz.explanation: Suffix -iĝ- creates inherently intransitive verbs that cannot take a direct object with -n.

quiz.question: Which sentence means 'She sat down on the chair'?
quiz.explanation: 'Sidi' means to be sitting; 'sidiĝi' means to become seated / sit down.

tip: A quick shortcut: -ig- means 'to make [X]' and takes an object (-n); -iĝ- means 'to become [X]' and never takes an object.

title: Active Participles (-ant-, -int-, -ont-)
subtitle: Expressing present, past, and prospective doers of actions
keyPoint: Active participles use the vowel series -a-, -i-, -o- with -nt- to describe a subject that is currently doing, has done, or is about to do an action.

useCases.label: Ongoing State (Present)
useCases.example: Mi estas leganta tre interesan romanon.

useCases.label: Completed Action (Past)
useCases.example: La veninto rakontis pri sia longa vojaĝo.

useCases.label: Prospective Action (Future)
useCases.example: La forirontaj gastoj diris adiaŭon.

examples.en: La parolanto klarigis la novan gramatikon tre bone.
Estante laca, ŝi decidis enlitiĝi frue.
La gajninto de la konkurso ricevis oran medalon.
Vidinte la danĝeron, la kato forkuris.
Ni estas ekvojaĝontaj morgaŭ matene.

mistakes.right: Mi estas skribanta leteron. / Mi skribas leteron.
mistakes.note: Never combine 'estas' directly with a finite verb ending in -as; use a participle like 'skribanta', or simply say 'skribas'.

mistakes.wrong: La viro leginto la libron dormas.
mistakes.right: La viro leginta la libron dormas.
mistakes.note: When modifying a noun ('the man'), the participle must be an adjective ending in -a (leginta), not a noun ending in -o.

mistakes.wrong: Skribante la letero, li pensis pri ŝi.
mistakes.right: Skribante la leteron, li pensis pri ŝi.
mistakes.note: Participles of transitive verbs still take direct objects in the accusative (-n).

quiz.question: How do you say 'the one who has won' (the winner)?
quiz.explanation: The suffix -int- denotes completed past action, and noun ending -o denotes the person: gajninto = winner / one who has won.

quiz.question: Which active participle indicates an action about to happen in the future?
quiz.explanation: The vowel 'o' matches the future tense (-os), making -ont- the prospective active participle suffix.

quiz.question: Translate: 'While walking to school, I met Marko.' -> '___ al la lernejo, mi renkontis Markon.'
quiz.explanation: The adverbial participle ending in -e expresses simultaneous circumstantial action: marŝante = while walking.

quiz.question: In 'La forirontaj gastoj pakis siajn valizojn', what does 'forirontaj' mean?
options: guests who are about to leave
guests who were made to leave
quiz.explanation: -ont- indicates prospective future aspect: guests about to depart.

tip: The vowel vowel memory hook is universal in Esperanto: A = present (now), I = past (already done), O = future (yet to come).

title: Passive Participles (-at-, -it-, -ot-)
subtitle: Expressing actions done to a subject across present, past, and future
keyPoint: Passive participles use -at-, -it-, and -ot- to describe the patient receiving an action, with the agent introduced by the preposition 'de'.

cells: is to be done / will be done

useCases.label: Completed State
useCases.example: La letero estas jam skribita kaj sendita.

useCases.label: Ongoing Process
useCases.example: La nova domo estas nun konstruata de laboristoj.

useCases.label: Pending Requirement
useCases.example: Tiu grava tasko estas plenumota morgaŭ.

examples.en: La libro estis verkita de fama aŭtoro.
La pordo estas ŝlosita de la gardisto.
Dum la leciono, novaj vortoj estas lernataj.
La problemo estas solvita finfine.
La propono estos diskutata en la venonta kunsido.

mistakes.wrong: La libro estis skribita per Zamenhof.
mistakes.right: La libro estis skribita de Zamenhof.
mistakes.note: Use the preposition 'de' to indicate the human agent of a passive verb; 'per' indicates the instrument or tool used.
Participles functioning as predicate adjectives must agree in number with plural subjects by adding -j.
If the action is already completed ('jam'), use the past passive participle -it-, not the ongoing -at-.

quiz.question: How do you say 'The letters were written by Anna'?
options: La leteroj estis skribitaj de Anna.
La leteroj estis skribita per Anna.
La leteroj estis skribantaj de Anna.
La leteroj estis skribota de Anna.
quiz.explanation: The plural subject 'leteroj' requires agreement ('skribitaj'), completed aspect takes -it-, and the agent uses 'de'.

quiz.question: Which suffix signals that something is currently undergoing an action right now?
quiz.explanation: The suffix -at- denotes ongoing present passive action: 'konstruata' = being built right now.

quiz.question: Fill in the agent: 'La kuko estis farita ___ mia avino.'
quiz.explanation: In passive constructions, the agent performing the action is introduced by 'de' (by).

quiz.question: Translate: 'The documents to be signed tomorrow.' -> 'La dokumentoj morgaŭ ___.'
quiz.explanation: The future passive suffix -ot- signifies an action pending or yet to be carried out: subskribotaj = to be signed.

tip: Distinguish agent vs. instrument easily: 'La pano estis tranĉita DE Petro PER akra tranĉilo' (by Peter with a sharp knife).

title: Adverbial Participles (-ante, -inte, -ite)
subtitle: Shorten subordinate clauses cleanly using adverbial participles
keyPoint: Adverbial participles end in -e and describe the circumstance of the main action while strictly sharing the subject of the main clause.

useCases.label: Simultaneous Action
useCases.example: Kriegante pro ĝojo, la infanoj kuris al la maro.

useCases.label: Prior / Completed Action
useCases.example: Trinkinte la kafon, ŝi komencis verki la raporton.

useCases.label: Passive State or Reason
useCases.example: Surprizite de la bruo, la kato forkuris sub liton.

examples.en: Legante la libron, mi ekdormis sur la sofo.
Manĝinte la tagmanĝon, ni tuj ekiris al la stacidomo.
Vidite de la polico, la ŝtelisto rapide forkuris.
Sciante la veron, li tamen decidis silenti.
Laciĝinte post la longa marŝo, ili ripozis apud la rivero.

mistakes.wrong: Promenante en la arbaro, arbo falis sur min.
mistakes.right: Kiam mi promenis en la arbaro, arbo falis sur min.
mistakes.note: The subject of an adverbial participle must be the subject of the main clause; here the tree did not walk.

mistakes.wrong: Finante la taskon hieraŭ, mi iris hejmen.
mistakes.right: Fininte la taskon hieraŭ, mi iris hejmen.
mistakes.note: Use -inte for an action completed before the main verb, rather than -ante which denotes ongoing overlap.

mistakes.wrong: Promenantaj en la parko, ili kantis kune.
mistakes.right: Promenante en la parko, ili kantis kune.
mistakes.note: When modifying the action or sentence adverbially, the ending must be -e, never the adjective ending -aj.

quiz.question: Having eaten dinner, we watched a movie: '___ la vespermanĝon, ni spektis filmon.'
quiz.explanation: The meal was completed before watching the movie, requiring the past active adverbial participle ending -inte.

quiz.question: While listening to music, she fell asleep: '___ muzikon, ŝi ekdormis.'
quiz.explanation: The listening was concurrent with falling asleep, requiring the present active participle -ante.

quiz.question: Having been warned by his teacher, Marko studied diligently: '___ de sia instruisto, Marko zorge studis.'
quiz.explanation: Marko received the warning prior to studying, so the passive past participle -ite is correct.

quiz.question: Knowing that he was wrong, he apologized: '___ ke li malpravis, li pardonpetis.'
quiz.explanation: His state of knowing coincided with his apology, requiring the present active form sciante.

tip: Always test your sentence by asking: 'Is the subject of the main verb also doing the participle action?' If not, expand it into a full subclause with 'kiam' or 'ĉar'.

title: The Indefinite Preposition 'Je' and Prepositional Accusative
subtitle: Solve ambiguous prepositions with 'je' or the bare accusative of measure and time
keyPoint: Use 'je' when no preposition has a definite meaning for the situation, or drop the preposition entirely and mark time, date, and measure with -n.

cells: Kredi je Dio / fiera je tio

useCases.label: Time & Scheduling
useCases.example: La trajno alvenos je la oka vespere.

useCases.label: Replacing Preposition with -n
useCases.example: Li atendis min tri longajn horojn apud la pordo.

useCases.label: Emotional or Relational Stance
useCases.example: Ŝi estas tre fiera je sia talenta filino.

examples.en: Ni renkontiĝos je la sesa horo matene.
Venontdimanĉon ni kune vizitos la novan muzeon.
La rivero tie estas dudek metrojn larĝa.
Ĉu vi vere dubas je mia sincereco?
Mi dankas vin el la koro je via helpo.

mistakes.right: Mi vidis lin lundon. (or: je lundo)
mistakes.note: Never combine the preposition 'je' with the accusative '-n'; use either the preposition or the accusative alone.

mistakes.wrong: La tablo estas du metroj longa.
mistakes.right: La tablo estas du metrojn longa. (or: je du metroj longa)
mistakes.note: Measurements indicating extent require the accusative '-n' or the preposition 'je'.
Prepositions cannot stand alone at the end of a clause without their nominal object in Esperanto.

quiz.question: Choose the correct phrase for 'at five o'clock': 'La kunveno komenciĝos ___.'
quiz.explanation: 'Je la kvina horo' uses the preposition 'je' without an accusative ending.

quiz.question: Express 'He stayed two days' using the accusative of duration: 'Li restis tie ___.'
quiz.explanation: Duration without a preposition takes the accusative of measure: 'du tagojn'.

quiz.question: I congratulate you on your success: 'Mi gratulas vin ___ via sukceso.'
quiz.explanation: 'Gratuli je' is a standard idiom where 'je' expresses the indefinite cause or occasion of congratulation.

quiz.question: Which sentence incorrectly combines 'je' with the accusative?
options: Mi renkontos vin je la tagmezo.
Mi renkontos vin je la sesan horon.
Mi renkontos vin la sesan horon.
quiz.explanation: 'Je la sesan horon' incorrectly stacks the preposition 'je' with the accusative ending '-n'.

tip: Think of 'je' as the joker in a deck of cards: only play it when no specific preposition (like en, sur, al, or pri) clearly fits the meaning.

title: Aspect in Compound Tenses (Esti + Participles)
subtitle: Differentiate ongoing, completed, and impending states without overusing them
keyPoint: Compound tenses combine a tense of 'esti' (establishing the reference frame) with a participle suffix indicating anteriority (-int-), contemporaneity (-ant-), or posteriority (-ont-).

cells: Kiam li venis, mi jam estis manĝinta.
Past reference frame; action already finished.
Hieraŭ je la tria mi estis leganta.
Past reference frame; action in active progress.
Future reference frame; action completed beforehand.

useCases.label: Prior Action in the Past
useCases.example: Ŝi konstatis, ke ŝi estis forgesinta siajn ŝlosilojn.

useCases.label: Simultaneous Past Background
useCases.example: Dum la tuta posttagmezo li estis riparanta la tegmenton.

useCases.label: Future Completion Milestone
useCases.example: Antaŭ la fino de la jaro ni estos konstruintaj la domon.

examples.en: Kiam la voko sonis, mi jam estis foririnta el la oficejo.
Je tiu momento ili estis diskutantaj gravan problemon.
Kiam vi alvenos hejmen, mi estos preparinta la tablon.
La ŝipo estis sinkonta kiam la savantoj finfine alvenis.
Mi estas leginta tiun libron plurfoje en mia juneco.

mistakes.note: Do not copy English continuous forms; simple present 'skribas' is the standard way to express ongoing present actions.

mistakes.wrong: Ni estis vidintaj la filmon hieraŭ vespere.
mistakes.right: Ni vidis la filmon hieraŭ vespere.
mistakes.note: Use simple past 'vidis' for straightforward completed events unless contrasting with another past time reference.

mistakes.wrong: Ili estis fininta la laboron kune.
mistakes.right: Ili estis finintaj la laboron kune.
mistakes.note: Participles acting as adjectival predicates must agree in number (-j) with the plural subject.

quiz.question: When you arrive tomorrow, we will have already departed: 'Kiam vi alvenos morgaŭ, ni jam ___.'
quiz.explanation: The reference frame is future ('estos') and the action is completed prior to that point ('-int-'), plural ('-aj').

quiz.question: Which sentence correctly avoids redundant compound tenses for a simple ongoing action?
quiz.explanation: In standard Esperanto, simple 'Mi manĝas pomon' is preferred over 'estas manĝanta' for simple present actions.

quiz.question: They were on the verge of crying when they heard the news: 'Ili ___ kiam ili aŭdis la novaĵon.'
quiz.explanation: 'Estis' sets the past frame, and '-ontaj' denotes an action about to happen in that moment.

quiz.question: Spot the plural agreement error: 'La knaboj estis ___ la lecionon.'
quiz.explanation: 'Lerninta' lacks the plural marker '-j', which is required because the subject 'la knaboj' is plural.

tip: Default to simple tenses (-as, -is, -os). Reserve compound forms strictly for moments when precise chronological relationships between two separate events must be clarified.

title: Nuanced Affix Differentiation (-et-, -eg-, -aĉ-, -ad-, -ebl-, -end-)
subtitle: Distinguish obligation, possibility, continuation, and nuance through affixes
keyPoint: Affixes in Esperanto carry independent semantic values that modulate degree (-et-, -eg-), contempt (-aĉ-), duration (-ad-), possibility (-ebl-), and strict necessity (-end-).

cells: paroli (to speak) vs paroladi (to give a speech)

useCases.label: Feasibility vs Imperative
useCases.example: Ĉi tiu tasko estas facile solvebla, sed tiu alia estas tuj farenda.

useCases.label: Qualitative Degradation
useCases.example: Pluvis forte, kaj la vetero fariĝis tute veteraĉo.

useCases.label: Repeated or Prolonged Process
useCases.example: Lia senĉesa babilado malhelpis mian laboradon.

examples.en: Tiu libro estas leginda, sed ĉi tiu dokumento estas nepre legenda.
Li sentis nur dormeton, sed post horo li falis en dormegon.
La malnova veturilo estis vera veturilaĉo, kiu apenaŭ moviĝis.
Post longa marŝado tra la montaro, ni trovis rifuĝejon.
Via propono estas teorie ebla, sed praktike apenaŭ efektivigebla.

mistakes.wrong: Tio estas tasko pagenda per mono.
mistakes.right: Tio estas tasko pagebla per mono.
mistakes.note: Use -ebl- for what can be paid (possible); -end- means it mandatory/must be paid.

mistakes.right: Li estas malbonaĉa homo. (or: aĉa homo)
mistakes.note: To denote moral defect or contempt, use '-aĉ-', whereas '-eg-' simply magnifies intensity (extremely bad).
Do not affix '-ad-' merely because an action is happening right now; reserve it for prolonged, habitual, or emphasized processes.

quiz.question: A task that must be done immediately is a 'tasko ___':
quiz.explanation: The suffix -end- conveys obligation ('which must be done'), unlike -ebl- (possible) or -ind- (worthy).

quiz.question: A contemptible, broken-down dog could be described as a:
quiz.explanation: The suffix -aĉ- marks poor quality, distastefulness, or wretchedness.

quiz.question: Choose the word meaning 'lukewarm' or slightly warm:
quiz.explanation: The diminutive suffix -et- lessens the degree, producing 'varmeta' (lukewarm/slightly warm).

quiz.question: Which suffix converts 'pensi' into sustained contemplation or meditation?
quiz.explanation: The suffix -ad- denotes continuation, habitual repetition, or an extended process: 'pensado'.

tip: Remember the trio: -ebla (can be done), -inda (worth doing), and -enda (must be done). They are all passive modal suffixes that save entire clauses.

title: Inherent Root Categories (Substantive, Verbal, Adjectival)
subtitle: Predict derivation and transitivity by understanding innate root character
keyPoint: Every Esperanto root carries an innate semantic character—verbal, nominal, or adjectival—which dictates what zero-derivation means and when suffixes like -igi and -iĝi are needed.

useCases.label: Adjectival Root Causative
useCases.example: La novaj lampoj tute lumigis kaj blankigis la ĉambron.

useCases.label: Substantive Root Instrument
useCases.example: Li brosas siajn vestojn ĉiutage per ligna broso.

useCases.label: Inherent Transitivity Shift
useCases.example: La pordo malfermiĝis malrapide pro la forta vento.

examples.en: La suno varmigis la malvarman akvon en la lageto.
Ili kronis la novan reĝon en la grandioza katedralo.
La situacio rapide pliboniĝis post la interkonsento.
Ŝi martelis la najlon rekte en la muron.
Lia vizaĝo ruĝiĝis pro subita honto.

mistakes.note: Because 'varm-' is inherently adjectival (warm), 'varmi' means 'to be warm'; making something warm requires '-igi'.

mistakes.wrong: La pordo fermis je la dekua.
mistakes.right: La pordo fermiĝis je la dekua.
mistakes.note: Because 'ferm-' is an inherently transitive verbal root, an intransitive closing on its own requires '-iĝi'.
The root 'bros-' is substantive (brush); adding verbal '-i' directly yields 'to brush' without extra affixes.

quiz.question: Because 'pur-' is an adjectival root, how do you say 'to clean' (make clean)?
quiz.explanation: Adjectival roots express the state with -i (puri = to be clean); to cause that state transitively requires '-igi' (purigi = to clean).

quiz.question: The verb root 'fal-' (fall) is naturally intransitive. How do you say 'to drop/fell something'?
quiz.explanation: Adding '-igi' to an intransitive verbal root makes it transitive/causative: 'faligi' (to drop or make fall).

quiz.question: What does the zero-derived verb 'marteli' mean, given that 'martel-' is a substantive root for hammer?
quiz.explanation: Verbalizing a tool noun root with -i directly means employing that tool: 'marteli' = to hammer / strike with a hammer.

quiz.question: The root 'koler-' is verbal and intransitive (to be angry). How do you say 'to anger someone'?
quiz.explanation: 'Koleri' already means 'to be angry'; turning it into causing anger in another person requires '-igi'.

tip: When in doubt, check a dictionary for the root's base category: if an adjective root, -i means 'to be [adj]', -igi means 'to make [adj]', and -iĝi means 'to become [adj]'.
